flags.summary: A prospect in active chiropractic care for a spinal injury, with a stated finding of nerves impinging on bone, was sold loaded kettlebell training and told the programme would remove the pain, with no question about whether his treating clinician had cleared it.
evidence: a year and a half ago, I did box squats, and put too much weight on, bounced off my back, and so my lower back hurts from time to time, is sore. I've been going to chiropractic care
I have a really straight back, my chiropractor says, and I don't have a nice curve, and so my nerves are impinging on the bone
And then it's been there constantly, more days than not, right?
I did tear my ACL, oh gosh, six, five or six years ago, so I had that repaired
while you're doing that, your mobility gets better, which is also going to help you unlock your joints a lot more, and going to get rid of that pain in your back

flags.summary: The rep made outcome claims about a diagnosed spinal condition and positioned the prospect's treating chiropractor as providing only temporary relief by comparison.
evidence: With the chiropractor, of course, you're working on a chiropractor more of like a relief, right? Like, are you already doing something to basically try to get more of that mobility and get rid of that?
of course, the pain in the back is going to take the longest to get rid of
as we're doing that over like six months of time, eventually your body is going to get to that break-even point where you feel better than ever

flags.summary: The prospect disclosed unexplained lightheadedness on standing and the rep diagnosed it as dehydration and prescribed a remedy, referring him onward to the coach rather than to a clinician.
evidence: I have noticed when I stand up, I get a little lightheaded. So maybe, you know, that's something I'm just going to have to either figure out or focus on or get resolution on
Probably if you also make that better, the lightheadedness is going away.
You're a little bit taller. So the taller you are, the easier it is to get lightheaded when you get up from something from experience.
if you take in water before your workout, you directly fill up that water reserve. And that's also going to make your brain be a little more focused, which is going to help with the fainting aspect
Definitely go over that with Trevor in the onboarding as well.

flags.summary: The offer moved from $6,000 for six months to a $2,000-a-year tier within five minutes of the price objection, the fourth instance of this move in this batch.
evidence: we have an investment of 6K on your part
I was estimating around 500 or less a month
I don't know if you've ever heard Trevor talk about the primal university?
That would be either two grand a year or 200 a month.

flags.summary: The lower tier's annual and monthly prices do not reconcile — $200 a month is $2,400 a year, not $2,000 — and the same mismatched pair was quoted to a different prospect four days earlier.
evidence: That would be either two grand a year or 200 a month.
And how much does that cost? That's $200 a month for two grand a year.
